payload.description_html:
Skeletal reconstruction of Austrocheirus isasii, a strange theropod from the Late Cretaceous Cerro Fortaleza Formation of Argentina. This particular reconstruction is based on a Berthasaurid position following Hendrickx et al., but the relationships of this species are still under debate. Based on the holotype MMPM-PV 10003, consisting of fragmentary hindlimb, forelimb, and vertebral elements. Unknown material filled in using Berthasaura, Gualicho, Deltadromeus, and vespersaurus. Total length is approximately 5.8 m through the centra.

Notes: Ulna is mirrored from the right side. Location of the pedal phalanxes and vertebral fragments is speculative. Measurements are unavailable for the manual ungual and fourth metatarsal, so their size is based on other elements and comparison with other specimens.

References: Ezcurra, 2010, Agnolín et. al., 2023, de Souza et. al., 2018, Langer et. al., 2019, and Apesteguía et. al., 2016.
